ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The molecule in the figure can be read as H3C–C(=O)–O–H. The leftmost carbon atom is connected to three hydrogen atoms: one H on the left, one H above, and one H below; at the same time it is also connected by a single bond to the carbon atom on the right. The carbon atom on the right forms a double bond with the oxygen atom above, and is connected to the O–H on the right. Reasoning: The question asks only about the leftmost carbon atom. Around this carbon atom there are four single bonds, that is, four bonding electron domains, and there are no lone pairs on the carbon. According to VSEPR theory, four bonding electron domains and no lone pairs correspond to a molecular geometry that is tetrahedral.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the molecule is drawn as H3C–C(=O)–O–H, and the left-most carbon is the CH3 carbon attached to three hydrogens and one neighboring carbon. From the question, focus only on that left-most carbon. Count its attached atoms/electron domains: four single bonds and no lone pairs on carbon. Use VSEPR to map four bonding domains around carbon to a tetrahedral molecular geometry. Answer: tetrahedral.
